anomalies.observed: Q10 is the only low-side path for the VSS pins of all seven WS2812B LEDs, but its metadata specifies a 190 mA NMOS.
anomalies.expected: The WS2812B ground switch should be rated for the total LED current; seven WS2812B devices can require well over 190 mA (up to roughly 420 mA at full white).
anomalies.impact: If the addressable LEDs are driven at moderate to full brightness, Q10 can overheat, current-limit, or fail, causing the LED chain to behave differently or be damaged.

anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have both GND1 and GND2 pins connected to the same system GND net.
anomalies.expected: For the intended isolated CAN buses, the transceiver secondary ground (GND2) should not be tied directly to the primary/system ground; isolation requires separate ground references.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The CAN interfaces would not provide the intended galvanic isolation, changing noise/safety behavior from the specified architecture.

anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW contains only the anodes of LEDs D4, D14, and D23, with no power source or driver connected to it.
anomalies.expected: An LED anode power net should be connected to a 3.3 V source or a switch/driver that can supply the LEDs; otherwise the LEDs cannot light.
anomalies.impact: D4, D14, and D23 will remain dark even when their cathode-side signals are active.

parsed.summary: The design files support at least one real anomaly: the WS2812 ground switch Q10 is undersized for the LED current it carries. The isolated CAN transceiver grounds are also merged with system ground, and a 3.3 V LED power net is left floating, both of which deviate from intended or standard behavior.
